requirement: EPIC-3 · Story 3.1 — Grid editor (hand-correction). Make every part of a lesson editable on the shared 32-step grid so a user can turn a rough reduce() draft (or an empty pattern) into a correct, playable lesson. Two capabilities are missing today and are the scope of this story: (1) set/adjust ANY bass note's pitch (native pad) and octave per step — today a bass cell can only be placed with the last-tapped pad at the live octave, or cleared; there is no per-note pitch/octave editing; (2) pattern PLAYBACK — the loop today only plays the metronome click and drives the visual playhead, it does NOT sound the stored drum hits / bass notes, so an edit cannot be heard 'in playback'. Add audio-time sequencing of the stored pattern so edits are audible immediately while looping. Drum add/remove already works via per-lane cell toggle (kick/snare/hat lanes) — do NOT rebuild it. ALL timing stays on Tone.Transport / Tone.Draw (no setInterval). Reuse the existing pattern.ts helpers (setBass = the setBassNote contract, clearBass = bass clearStep) and audio.ts (players/bass Sampler/playPad) — add no new audio path, no new dependency, no new sample.

architecture.decision: No design fork. The data model is the already-locked Lesson schema, realized by the existing in-memory Pattern store (src/pattern.ts): drums { kick|snare|hat: boolean[32] } + bass (BassCell|null)[32] with BassCell = { pad: PadId; octave: number; length: number }. Story 3.1 only EXTENDS the existing grid + adds an audio-time sequencer; it introduces no new format. The documented 3.1 state contract (setBassNote(step,pad,octave,length), clearStep(step,layer), toggleDrumHit(step,sound)) is already satisfied by pattern.ts: setBass IS setBassNote, clearBass IS bass clearStep, toggleDrum IS toggleDrumHit / drum clearStep. Reuse them; do not rename (ripples through App capture) and do not add one-caller aliases.
seams: src/transport.ts gains a SECOND step-subscriber set that fires at AUDIO time (not inside Tone.Draw): onStepAudio(cb: (step:number, time:number) => void): () => void, dispatched from inside the existing 16n scheduleRepeat BEFORE the Tone.Draw.schedule paint dispatch, passing the Tone audio `time`. This is the sequencing clock for pattern playback. It coexists with the existing onStep (visual, Tone.Draw) and onBeat — same Transport, phase-aligned, reset on start/stop. No second Transport, no setInterval. Visual onStep stays exactly as-is.

src/App.tsx owns pattern playback: a patternRef (kept in sync with the pattern state, like the existing stepRef) so the audio-time callback reads the CURRENT pattern with no stale closure; on each audio step it triggers, at the given audio `time`, every filled drum lane's Tone.Player and the bass note if the step has a BassCell. This is the full-mix default (all layers sound); EPIC-4 4.1 layer-gating chooses WHICH layers sound and layers on top of this — do not build gating here.

src/audio.ts gains time-accurate trigger entry points so playback can schedule on the audio thread: a way to start a drum Player at a specific Tone time and trigger the bass Sampler at a specific time (e.g. playDrumAt(sound, time) and playBassAt(pad, octave, time), or extend playPad with an optional time). Reuse the existing players/bass instances — no new samples, no new routing. Immediate tap/edit playback (no time arg) keeps working unchanged.

Bass note editor: a compact BassInspector surface (new src/BassInspector.tsx + css) edits the currently-selected bass step — a native-pad pitch picker (PAD_IDS) + an octave stepper (clampOctave, -2..+2) + a Remove button. src/StepGrid.tsx gains a selectedBassStep prop + onSelectBass callback and an is-selected visual on the chosen bass cell; App owns selectedBassStep state. Bass-cell click selects (empty cell first places a default note using lastPad/octave, then selects); editing in the inspector calls setBass (pitch/octave) + auditions the note + updates the grid label; Remove calls clearBass + deselects. Drum-cell click behavior is unchanged. Uses setBass/clearBass — no new pattern helper.

tasks.title: Pattern audio playback — sequence stored hits on the audio thread so edits are heard in the loop
tasks.intent: Make the looping transport SOUND the stored pattern (it currently plays only the metronome click + visual playhead). 1) src/transport.ts: add a second step-subscriber set fired at AUDIO time. Inside the EXISTING 16n scheduleRepeat callback, BEFORE the existing Tone.Draw.schedule(...) visual dispatch, iterate a new stepAudioSubscribers set calling cb(currentStep, time) with the Tone audio `time` passed into the repeat callback. Export onStepAudio(cb: (step:number, time:number) => void): () => void mirroring the existing onStep/onBeat (add to set, return unsubscribe). Do NOT touch the existing onStep (visual, dispatched in Tone.Draw) — both fire from the same repeat, phase-aligned. Reset behavior is unchanged (step already resets to 0 on start/stop). 2) src/audio.ts: add time-accurate trigger entry points that reuse the EXISTING players/bass instances: playDrumAt(sound: 'kick'|'snare'|'hat', time: number) that does players[sound].stop(time).start(time), and playBassAt(pad: PadId, octave: number, time: number) that does bass.triggerAttackRelease(bassNote(pad, octave), '8n', time). Both no-op if !isStarted(). Keep the existing playPad (immediate, no time) working unchanged. 3) src/App.tsx: add a patternRef (useRef) kept in sync with the pattern state on every setPattern (mirror the existing stepRef pattern — update the ref wherever pattern changes, or in a useEffect([pattern])). Subscribe once (useEffect, []) to transport.onStepAudio: on each (step, time), read patternRef.current and for that step trigger playDrumAt for each of kick/snare/hat whose lane[step] is true, and playBassAt(cell.pad, cell.octave, time) if pattern.bass[step] is non-null. This makes the whole stored pattern audible while looping and any edit audible on the very next pass. Do NOT add layer-gating (which layers play) — that is EPIC-4 4.1; here all layers sound.
tasks.constraints: ALL timing via Tone.Transport; the audio-step callback fires from the EXISTING 16n scheduleRepeat — NO setInterval / setTimeout / requestAnimationFrame, NO second Transport, NO new Tone.getTransport() scheduling loop. Trigger sounds at the passed audio `time` (sample-accurate) — do NOT schedule pattern audio inside Tone.Draw (that is paint time and will be late/jittery). patternRef MUST avoid stale closures (the once-registered subscriber has to see the latest pattern). Reuse the existing Tone.Player 'kick'/'snare'/'hat' and the bass Tone.Sampler + bassNote() — add NO new sample, NO new dependency, NO new routing. Keep tap/edit immediate playback (playPad) working. TypeScript strict, no unused symbols. Keep existing ponytail comments; add a ponytail comment noting all-layers-play is the default and EPIC-4 4.1 adds layer gating. Extend a _selfcheck only if you add pure logic; do not add audio to _selfcheck.
tasks.acceptance: npm run build passes. transport.ts exports onStepAudio((step,time)=>void):()=>void alongside the unchanged onStep/onBeat/startTransport/stopTransport/etc. audio.ts exports playDrumAt and playBassAt reusing the existing instances. In the browser: with a non-empty pattern and PLAY running, the stored kick/snare/hat hits and bass notes are AUDIBLE at their steps in time with the click; toggling a cell (or editing a bass note) while looping is heard on the next loop pass. grep of src shows no setInterval/setTimeout/rAF used for timing. No console/audio-context errors.

Confirm audibly the pattern plays back in time with the metronome (observe no console errors; if audio can't be confirmed in the pane, verify via transport step logging that the audio callback fires at each step and calls the trigger fns, and screenshot the looping grid). tasks.title: Bass note editor — set/adjust any bass note's pitch (pad) + octave per step via a BassInspector
tasks.intent: Add per-step bass pitch/octave editing (today a bass cell can only be placed with the last pad/live octave, or cleared — no way to adjust an existing note's pitch/octave). 1) src/StepGrid.tsx: add props selectedBassStep: number | null and onSelectBass: (step:number)=>void. Give the currently-selected bass cell an is-selected visual (a non-color outline/ring cue, consistent with the playhead's non-color treatment). Bass-cell click now calls onSelectBass(step) instead of the current place-or-clear toggle; drum-cell click is UNCHANGED (still onToggleCell). Keep showing the pad label in a filled bass cell; optionally show a small octave indicator. 2) src/App.tsx: add selectedBassStep state. Bass-cell handling: clicking an EMPTY bass cell first places a default note { pad: lastPad ?? '1', octave: liveOctave, length: 1 } via setBass + auditions it, THEN selects that step; clicking a FILLED bass cell just selects it (and auditions its pitch). 3) new src/BassInspector.tsx + src/BassInspector.css: rendered (in the structure pane, near the grid) only when selectedBassStep != null and that step has a BassCell. Shows: the step number; a pitch picker over PAD_IDS (12 native pads as small labeled buttons, current pad highlighted); an octave stepper (-/readout/+ using clampOctave, disabled at -2/+2 ends, mirroring TransportControls' octave stepper); and a Remove button. Changing pad or octave calls setBass(step, { pad, octave, length }) (preserve existing length) AND auditions the new note (playPad bass) so the change is heard immediately AND updates the grid label; Remove calls clearBass(step) + clears selection. All controls are real, keyboard-focusable, ≥44px targets (a11y baseline from story 1.6), each with an aria-label; the inspector has an accessible group label. Reuse setBass/clearBass from pattern.ts (setBass = the setBassNote contract) — add NO new pattern helper. Do NOT regress drum editing, playhead sync, REC capture, or pattern playback from T1.
tasks.constraints: Reuse pattern.ts setBass/clearBass (immutable) — the setBassNote/clearStep contract is already these; do NOT add aliases or a new helper. Reuse audio.ts playPad(pad,{mode:'bass',octave}) for auditioning — no new audio path. Reuse clampOctave (constants.ts) as the single octave clamp — do not re-implement the range. a11y is non-negotiable (story 1.6 lock): every control keyboard-focusable + labeled, ≥44px .tbtn-style targets, the selected-cell cue is NOT hue-alone (outline/ring + shape), inspector has a group label, reduced-motion respected. Stealth theme + Anthropic-orange accent, match theme.css tokens (reuse existing .tbtn / control styles where possible instead of new bespoke CSS). Keep the diff minimal, TypeScript strict, mark deliberate shortcuts with a ponytail comment. The grid + inspector must work with an empty pattern and while stopped, and must not break when selectedBassStep points at a step whose note was just removed (guard null).
tasks.acceptance: npm run build passes. In the browser: clicking a bass cell selects it (visible non-color selected cue) without destroying it; the BassInspector appears and lets you (a) change the note's pitch by picking any of the 12 native pads — the grid cell label updates and the new pitch is heard; (b) raise/lower its octave with the stepper (clamped -2..+2, ends disabled) — heard immediately; (c) Remove the note — cell clears and selection ends. Adjusting pitch/octave of an EXISTING note works (not just placing a new one). Drum add/remove, playhead sync, REC capture, and T1 pattern playback all still work. All inspector controls are keyboard-operable and labeled. No console errors.
